controls.title: No Stripe secret, restricted or webhook key is committed
controls.statement: No Stripe secret key, restricted key or webhook signing secret (the sk_live_, sk_test_, rk_live_, rk_test_ and whsec_ prefixes) appears in source or committed config. The server reads each key from its environment at run time or from a secret store. A key in a committed file fails, because anyone with read access to the repository or its history can charge, refund or read customer data with it.
controls.look_for: A literal value after one of the five prefixes in code, config, tests, fixtures or docs; a key passed as a default value to an environment lookup.

controls.title: Every .env file is git-ignored and only .env.example is committed
controls.statement: Every .env file is listed in .gitignore and absent from the tree. A committed .env.example holds variable names only, each with an empty value or a placeholder that is not a key. A tracked .env file, or a .env.example holding a real value, fails, because the keys in it reach every clone.
controls.look_for: No .env line in .gitignore; a .env or .env.<name> file in git ls-files; a value after the equals sign in .env.example that carries a Stripe key prefix.

controls.title: Webhook handlers verify the Stripe signature before reading the event
controls.statement: Every Stripe webhook handler verifies the Stripe-Signature header with constructEvent (Node) or Webhook.construct_event (Python) against the raw request body, before it reads any field of the event. A handler that parses the body first, or skips the check, fails, because anyone who finds the endpoint can then forge a paid event.
controls.look_for: A webhook route that reads req.body or request.json before the signature check; a body parser that consumes the raw body before constructEvent; a handler with no signature check.

controls.title: Only the publishable key reaches client code
controls.statement: Client code holds only the publishable key (the pk_ prefix). A secret or restricted key prefix in client source, or a secret key exposed through a client build variable (VITE_, NEXT_PUBLIC_, REACT_APP_ or PUBLIC_), fails, because every visitor can read the shipped bundle.
controls.look_for: A secret key prefix in browser code; a client build variable whose name holds SECRET; a server key imported into a module the client bundle includes.

controls.title: The server sets every amount and currency
controls.statement: The amount and currency of every charge, payment intent or checkout session come from the server's own catalog or from Stripe price ids. An amount, unit_amount or currency taken from the client request fails, because a player can then pay any price for any item.
controls.look_for: unit_amount, amount or currency read from req.body, request.json or a query string; price_data built from client input instead of a server-side lookup.
